bundleSuggestion: CONSPIRACY_THEORY + HISTORY — pairs with KAYFABIZARRO-5 Hidden History and KAYFABIZARRO CONSPIRACY Akashic Archive

cards.power: Descent. Discard your hand to draw three "Theory" cards. No going back.
cards.lore: "The entry point is usually a photograph that doesn't make sense. Or a golf course built on a palace."
cards.gradeReason: Discard everything, draw Theory cards, no going back — you ARE the rabbit hole.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Vintage conspiracy collage, sepia. Subject: Hand releasing cards into bottomless spiral. Mood: Irreversible descent.

cards.lore: "I'm not saying it's a conspiracy. I'm saying 75,000 workers don't just vanish into thin air. Stay fluffy!"
cards.gradeReason: Iconic lore but no performance instruction — you appreciate it, you don't embody it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: 1890s newspaper illustration. Subject: Giant empty construction site, lone figure. Mood: Bureaucratic erasure.

cards.power: Choice. Player chooses: Believe the Official Narrative (skip turn) OR Question Reality (draw 2).
cards.lore: "Warning: Side effects include skepticism, insomnia, and obsession with mud."
cards.gradeReason: Binary performance choice with immediate mechanical stakes — you play the scene at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian apothecary poster. Subject: Two pills on velvet, one red one blue. Mood: Theatrically irreversible.

cards.lore: "History is a collage. Sometimes you have to make the cuts." Physically cut these cards out to play the game. Destroy the evidence.
cards.gradeReason: The instruction IS the card. Cutting the cards = destroying the evidence. Pure meta-performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dada collage, torn edges. Subject: Ornate scissors mid-cut through official document. Mood: Gleeful sabotage.

cards.power: Haste. Build any "Monument" card instantly without paying the resource cost.
cards.lore: "From swamp to 200 neoclassical palaces in two years. Mathematically dubious. Architecturally miraculous."
cards.gradeReason: Strong conceptual hook but Haste is a mechanic, not a role — the builder needs context to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Engraving, accelerated time-lapse. Subject: Palace rising from swamp at impossible speed. Mood: Dubious wonder.

cards.power: Scale. Occupy 44 acres of fair space. Blocks all other "Logic" cards.
cards.lore: "1,687 feet long. The largest roof in the world. A shed for giants, built by 'temporary' permits."
cards.gradeReason: Blocks Logic is a great mechanic, but the card reads as historical data — no role to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian blueprint, ghostly overlay. Subject: Vast shed roof stretching to horizon. Mood: Impossibly mundane.

cards.power: Labor Force. Generate massive output for one turn, then vanish from the game board entirely.
cards.lore: "An army the size of a city. No housing records. No sanitation records. Just ghosts with hammers."
cards.gradeReason: Generate everything then vanish — you become the undocumented labor force, then cease to exist.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Faded sepia photograph. Subject: Blurred crowd of workers, faces dissolving. Mood: Mass erasure.

cards.power: Assembly. Treat "Stone" cards as "Staff & Plaster" to reduce build cost to zero.
cards.lore: "They said it was iron and glass kits. Like IKEA, but for Roman Emperors."
cards.gradeReason: IKEA for Roman Emperors is a killer line but the mechanic is accounting, not performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Instruction manual parody, Victorian fonts. Subject: Flat-pack Roman column with hex key. Mood: Absurd competence.

cards.power: Inspiration. Draw the entire deck if you can explain how this was engineered in a week.
cards.lore: "Designed during a board meeting on a piece of blotting paper. Genius or download?"
cards.gradeReason: Brilliant challenge mechanic but drawing the deck requires a rules beat — not instant performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Chromolithograph, otherworldly light. Subject: Crystal Palace interior, impossible scale. Mood: Suspiciously beautiful.

cards.power: The Gardener. Transform a "Greenhouse" card into a "World Wonder."
cards.lore: "He grew lilies. Then he designed the future of architecture. It's a natural progression, obviously."
cards.gradeReason: Archetype is clear but the greenhouse-to-wonder transformation needs narrative scaffolding at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian botanical illustration. Subject: Gardener holding lily that transforms into crystal palace. Mood: Casual genius.

cards.power: Biomimicry. Strut against opponents.
cards.lore: "The gardener out-engineered the Royal Institute. It's a natural progression, obviously."
cards.gradeReason: The name alone tells you everything. You ARE the amphibian in formal wear strutting past the establishment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian portrait parody. Subject: Distinguished frog in top hat, confident posture. Mood: Smug outsider triumph.

cards.lore: "The building was 1,851 feet long. The year was 1851. Subtle, guys. Very subtle."
cards.gradeReason: Clever observation but no action instruction — you note the coincidence, you don't perform it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Architectural blueprint with red annotations. Subject: Length measurement overlaid on calendar year. Mood: Suspicious numerology.

cards.power: Material. Rapid construction. Structures dissolve if it rains for three turns.
cards.lore: "It looks like Rome. It feels like Rome. Just don't scratch the paint."
cards.gradeReason: Dissolves-in-rain is a great mechanic but you need table context to make the Rome bluff land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Rain-damaged classical painting. Subject: Ornate facade washing away to reveal bare wood. Mood: Theatrical impermanence.

cards.power: Standardization. All structures must look identical to the opponent's building.
cards.lore: "They all went to the same school. They all kept the same secret. They all built the same."
cards.gradeReason: Conformity mechanic is thematically rich but the enforcer role needs context to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Beaux-Arts blueprint, repeated pattern. Subject: Identical building facades stretching to vanishing point. Mood: Conspiratorial uniformity.

cards.lore: "...structure? Or is it a circuit..."
cards.gradeReason: OCR incomplete, title opaque — can't embody something you can't decode.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Esoteric architectural diagram. Subject: Building plan overlaid with circuit board. Mood: Hidden technology.

cards.gradeReason: OCR incomplete — card content not recoverable from this PDF rendering.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Architectural blueprint, aged. Subject: Ornate facade with hidden annotations. Mood: Institutional secrecy.

cards.power: Disaster. Destroy one "Tower" card. Gain sympathy points but lose the evidence.
cards.lore: "It burned during the fair. A spectacular warning of things to come."
cards.gradeReason: Gain sympathy, lose the evidence — you ARE the cover story, performing grief while hiding the arson.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: News illustration, fire and shadow. Subject: Tower in flames, crowd watching. Mood: Orchestrated tragedy.

cards.power: Blame. Sacrifice this card to explain away any massive structural collapse.
cards.lore: "History records that 'tramps' started the fire. Very efficient tramps."
cards.gradeReason: The sacrifice-to-explain mechanic is sharp but you need to play the scapegoat role against a real accusation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian newspaper crime illustration. Subject: Ragged figure holding match, accusatory pointing. Mood: Convenient villain.

cards.power: Wipe. Remove ALL "Temporary Buildings" from play. The board is now empty.
cards.lore: "Five months after closing. The most convenient fire in architectural history."
cards.gradeReason: Remove everything — the board is now empty. You perform the reset with a single gesture.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Before/after illustration, stark. Subject: Thriving fairground — then empty ash field. Mood: Methodical erasure.

cards.power: Liability. You pay nothing for the destruction of your own property.
cards.lore: "No insurance. No rebuilding. Just a clean slate for the golf course."
cards.gradeReason: Legal impunity is a role but the mechanic feels like an accountant's move rather than a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Legal document parody. Subject: Burning building with zero in insurance column. Mood: Cheerful impunity.

cards.power: Permanence. This card cannot be destroyed by Fire, Demolition, or Logic.
cards.lore: "The only one built to last. Because it housed the 'valuable' things."
cards.gradeReason: Immune to Logic. That's all. You embody the protected institution in a single phrase.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Classical museum engraving, fire raging around it. Subject: Serene museum standing amid destruction. Mood: Curated invulnerability.

cards.power: Curation. Keep the artifacts. Burn the blueprints.
cards.lore: "We kept the statues. We lost the knowledge of how we built the roof."
cards.gradeReason: Keep the artifacts, burn the blueprints — two gestures that make you the saboteur-archivist instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Library fire, selective lighting. Subject: Figure calmly holding artifacts while blueprints burn behind. Mood: Deliberate loss.

cards.power: Durability. Upgrade one building to "Permanent" status. It survives the reset.
cards.lore: "Why this one? Why brick here and plaster there? The decision that saved the museum."
cards.gradeReason: The survivability mechanic is solid but you need the table context to feel the weight of the choice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Material sample comparison diagram. Subject: Brick wall standing next to plaster rubble. Mood: Suspicious selection.

cards.power: Counter-Example. Prove that old things can survive if you don't burn them on purpose.
cards.lore: "Built 1811. Still standing. Proof that 'temporary' is a choice, not a law of physics."
cards.gradeReason: Academic debating move dressed as a card — Counter-Example is a lecture, not a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Annotated historical photograph. Subject: Old building dated 1811, circled with red pen. Mood: Inconvenient evidence.

cards.power: Transport. Move "Population" tokens from the East Coast to the Midwest.
cards.lore: "250,000 children. Shipped west. A repopulation effort or a humanitarian mission?"
cards.gradeReason: The dark history is immediately felt but 'move population tokens' is mechanical without the horror framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: 1890s train illustration, children at windows. Subject: Train loaded with children heading west. Mood: Ambiguous displacement.

cards.power: Origin. Cannot ask where the population came from.
cards.lore: "The polite fiction. Don't ask about the parents. Look at the vegetables."
cards.gradeReason: You perform the cover-up by playing a card that literally forbids the question. Pure institutional power.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian etiquette illustration. Subject: Cheerful scene, ominous blank space behind. Mood: Enforced ignorance.

cards.power: Display. Gain resources for every child placed in an exhibit.
cards.lore: "A building just for them. To be seen. To be managed. To be distributed."
cards.gradeReason: The horror is in the lore but the mechanic needs a beat to fully land as performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Fair exhibition poster, unsettling. Subject: Children in labeled rows under museum lighting. Mood: Managed humanity.

cards.power: Workforce. Convert "Orphan" cards into "Farm Hands."
cards.lore: "The farms needed hands. The trains provided them."
cards.gradeReason: Convert Orphan cards into Farm Hands — the transformation is the performance, moral weight included.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Administrative ledger illustration. Subject: Column labeled Orphan with arrow to Farm Hand. Mood: Efficient brutality.

cards.power: Defense. +10 Defense against cannons. +10 Theory Generation.
cards.lore: "Military base? Or circuit board stamped into the earth?"
cards.gradeReason: Dual nature question is evocative but the double-bonus mechanic keeps you in game-manager mode.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Aerial map overlay, circuit board. Subject: Star fort geometry echoing printed circuit. Mood: Encoded purpose.

cards.power: Resonance. Harvest "Aether" from the atmosphere if your geometry is perfect.
cards.lore: "Sound creates form. Did they build the fort, or did the frequency build it for them?"
cards.gradeReason: Harvest Aether is atmospheric but 'if your geometry is perfect' requires a rule check, not a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Esoteric frequency diagram. Subject: Sound waves emanating from fort geometry. Mood: Sacred acoustics.

cards.power: Crossfire. Eliminate any unit entering the geometry.
cards.lore: "The official story: It's about shooting people better. No dead zones."
cards.gradeReason: Clean mechanic but you're the fort designer, not someone you can feel yourself becoming at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Military diagram, cold precision. Subject: Overlapping fields of fire from angled bastions. Mood: Calculated lethality.

cards.power: Focus. Direct all energy to a single point.
cards.lore: "A spear tip made of masonry. Pointing at what?"
cards.gradeReason: The question ending is great but 'direct all energy' is a utility power without a clear body to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Architectural drawing with directional arrows. Subject: Angular fort tip pointing toward distant target. Mood: Directed menace.

cards.power: Terraform. Turn "Swamp" tiles into "Grand Canal."
cards.lore: "They didn't just build buildings. They built a hydraulic civilization on a swamp."
cards.gradeReason: Impressive concept but terraforming tiles is a background action — no one to be at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Engineering cross-section diagram. Subject: Swamp transforming into canal system below city. Mood: Civilizational scale.

cards.power: Excavation. Move the mud. Hide the basement.
cards.lore: "Moving the earth to make the water flow. The scale of the digging matches the scale of the building."
cards.gradeReason: Move the mud. Hide the basement. Two commands that make you the cover-up engineer immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Underground cross-section illustration. Subject: Workers moving mud, hidden chamber below. Mood: Systematic concealment.

cards.power: Sanctuary. A place of nature amidst the plaster.
cards.lore: "Olmsted's fictional nature that looks more real than the buildings."
cards.gradeReason: Poetic contrast but Sanctuary is a passive buff — you appreciate the illusion, you don't perform it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Landscape painting, pastoral. Subject: Lush garden beside stark plaster facade. Mood: Artificial serenity.

cards.power: Foundation. Build on unstable ground. Ignore "sinking" penalties for 2 turns.
cards.lore: "San Francisco. Always building on the mud. Always claiming it's new."
cards.gradeReason: Ignoring sinking penalties is the most mechanical description of a conspiracy card in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Engineering report parody. Subject: Building tilting into mud, foundation stamp says APPROVED. Mood: Willful blindness.

cards.power: Capacity. Hold infinite "Tech" cards.
cards.lore: "The largest enclosed space in the world. 1,378 feet of impossible iron."
cards.gradeReason: Hold infinite Tech is a storage mechanic — impressive but passive, no archetype to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Industrial engraving, cathedral scale. Subject: Vast iron and glass interior with rows of machines. Mood: Impossible engineering.

cards.power: Broadcast. Transmit the signal globally. Win the "Attention" war.
cards.lore: "The one they kept. The spire. The lightning rod for the world."
cards.gradeReason: Win the Attention war is vivid but broadcast is a mechanic — you operate the tower, you don't become it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Vintage postcard, signal waves. Subject: Eiffel Tower emitting radio waves across globe. Mood: Imperial attention.

cards.power: Vandalism. Destroy a World Wonder to make room for a lawn.
cards.lore: "Rodin called it a crime. They tore it down for a view. We lost the space."
cards.gradeReason: Destroy a World Wonder to make room for a lawn. Rodin called it a crime. You're the philistine instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Demolition photograph, indifferent officials. Subject: Wrecking ball hitting glass palace, lawn beyond. Mood: Cultural murder.

cards.power: Mobility. Move units across the board without expending energy.
cards.lore: "1893 tech. We still struggle with airport walkways. They had it perfect."
cards.gradeReason: Great lore question, flattest possible power name — Mobility with no-cost movement is a logistics card, not a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: 1890s technology illustration. Subject: Passengers gliding on moving platform, amazed faces. Mood: Suppressed future.

cards.power: Illumination. Reveal all hidden cards in opponent's hand.
cards.lore: "Edison's monument. 5,000 bulbs. A pillar of fire without the heat."
cards.gradeReason: Reveal opponent's hand is strong but Illumination as Edison tribute needs the Tesla context to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Exhibition illustration, dramatic lighting. Subject: 82-foot column of incandescent bulbs blazing. Mood: Corporate spectacle.

cards.power: Current. Power the entire city. Render "DC" cards obsolete.
cards.lore: "The war of currents ended here. AC won. The machines that proved it are gone."
cards.gradeReason: Power the city, render DC obsolete — you ARE Tesla winning the war, then losing the machines.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Electrical diagram, triumphant. Subject: AC motor powering cityscape, DC cables going dark. Mood: Victory and erasure.

cards.power: Suppression. Cancel the effect of an opponent's "Invention" card.
cards.lore: "We have the idea. We don't have the schematic. Lost in the archives."
cards.gradeReason: Cancel their invention — you are the corporate suppressor making knowledge disappear. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Archive photograph, redacted. Subject: Patent filing with key pages absent, stamp ARCHIVED. Mood: Institutional theft.

cards.power: Speed. Instant delivery of resources.
cards.lore: "Compressed air. The internet of matter. Why did we stop using this?"
cards.gradeReason: Great lore question, flattest possible power name — Speed with instant delivery is a logistics card, not a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Technical cross-section illustration. Subject: Underground tube network beneath city streets. Mood: Abandoned future.

cards.power: Reinterpretation. Flip a "Construction" card to reveal "Archaeology."
cards.lore: "Are they building the foundation? Or clearing the mud off the roof?"
cards.gradeReason: Flip construction to archaeology is conceptually brilliant but needs the key question read aloud to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Archaeological photograph, annotated. Subject: Construction site with classical column emerging from mud. Mood: Reversed time.

cards.power: Contrast. Reduce the area of a building by pointing out the dirt.
cards.lore: "Marble palaces. Mud roads. The dissonance of the 'reset.'"
cards.gradeReason: The dissonance observation is sharp but reducing building area by pointing at dirt needs table context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: 1893 photograph contrast. Subject: Grand white facade behind unpaved mud road. Mood: Cognitive dissonance.

cards.power: Silence. Skip the "Crowd" phase. No income this turn.
cards.lore: "Where are the people? 27 million visitors, but the photos are empty."
cards.gradeReason: Skip the crowd — the silence IS the performance. Absence as conspiracy is felt without any explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Long-exposure photograph, eerie. Subject: Grand boulevard completely empty, blurred ghost shapes. Mood: Photographic absence.

cards.power: Blur. Make your units untargetable for one turn.
cards.lore: "The official explanation: The exposure was too long. The people became ghosts."
cards.gradeReason: The ghost metaphor is perfect but Blur as untargetability is a protection mechanic — you don't become the ghost.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Long-exposure photography simulation. Subject: Crowd of white blur shapes in empty corridor. Mood: Official explanation.

cards.power: Legality. Destroy your own building to avoid maintenance costs.
cards.lore: "It was meant to die. That's why we killed it. Logic!"
cards.gradeReason: Destroy your own building to avoid costs. 'Logic!' You're the developer. You feel it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Legal document with wrecking ball imagery. Subject: Building demolition permit stamped APPROVED. Mood: Cheerful self-destruction.

cards.power: Audit. Force opponent to show their resources.
cards.lore: "Follow the money. It leads to banks. Banks are boring. Conspiracy over."
cards.gradeReason: The lore undermines itself and the mechanic — Audit is the most boring conspiracy action in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian accountant's ledger. Subject: Column of bank names, trailing off into boredom. Mood: Anticlimactic truth.

cards.power: Debunk. Cancel a "Conspiracy" card effect by citing a textbook.
cards.lore: "Actually, looking at the primary sources... (audience falls asleep)"
cards.gradeReason: The self-aware lore is beautiful but Debunk-by-citation is the most performatively inert role in this deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Academic lecture parody. Subject: Professor at podium, audience slumped asleep. Mood: Institutional sedation.

cards.power: Cause. The smallest object destroys the largest object.
cards.lore: "How did the steel building burn? One match. Very flammable steel."
cards.gradeReason: One match, very flammable steel. The sarcasm is the performance. You know the cover story, you play it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Crime scene illustration. Subject: Single lit match beside enormous steel skeleton. Mood: Impossible causation.

cards.power: Facade. Your units appear stronger than they are. Bluffing +10.
cards.lore: "The civilization was performing itself. It wasn't real marble. It was a set."
cards.gradeReason: Bluffing +10 on a facade card. You're performing civilization. The meta-layer is instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Theater backstage reveal. Subject: Roman facade cracking to reveal plaster and wood behind. Mood: Civilization as performance.

cards.power: Narrative Control. Rewrite the history of one turn.
cards.lore: "The story the fair told: We are the peak. Everyone else is the past."
cards.gradeReason: Rewrite the history of one turn — you pick up the pen of empire and use it at the table, instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: History textbook illustration, editorial revision marks. Subject: Timeline being rewritten by unseen hand. Mood: Narrative authority.

cards.power: Context. Shame the opponent. Reduce their "Moral Authority" to zero.
cards.lore: "The people who funded the fair put the people they conquered in the zoo."
cards.gradeReason: The historical indictment is devastating but shame-the-opponent needs a setup beat to land as performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Exhibition catalog, clinical. Subject: Human figures labeled and categorized in display case. Mood: Colonial curation.

cards.power: Commodity. Trade your "Memory" for "Cash."
cards.lore: "The only thing that survives the fire is the merchandise."
cards.gradeReason: Trade Memory for Cash. The only thing that survives the fire is the merchandise. Final move, instantly understood.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Souvenir shop illustration, rubble background. Subject: Gift shop selling World's Fair trinkets, city in ash behind. Mood: Commerce as conclusion.

cards.power: Connection. Link two unrelated cards to create a combo effect.
cards.lore: "It all connects. If you use enough string."
cards.gradeReason: You're the conspiracy theorist with the bulletin board. Universal archetype, zero explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Conspiracy bulletin board, dense. Subject: Red string connecting newspaper clippings in pattern. Mood: Paranoid geometry.

cards.power: Protection. Immune to "Official Explanations" and "Mind Control."
cards.lore: "Shiny side out. Deflects logic rays."
cards.gradeReason: Immune to Official Explanations. Shiny side out. You know the hat, you know the role, no context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: How-to manual parody. Subject: Step-by-step tinfoil hat construction diagram, technical precision. Mood: Joyful paranoia.

cards.power: Cohesion. Repair a hole in your theory.
cards.lore: "When the facts don't hold together, use glue."
cards.gradeReason: Repair-a-hole is a passive fix mechanic — you're the handyman, not someone with a role to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: DIY repair manual. Subject: Theory diagram with glue poured over cracked section. Mood: Structural denial.

cards.power: Victory. If you spot 5 tropes in a row, shout "KAYFABINGO!" and flip the table.
cards.lore: "We're all playing it. Some of us just know the rules."
cards.gradeReason: Shout KAYFABINGO and flip the table. The instruction IS the game. Ultimate G1 by definition.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Bingo card parody. Subject: TVTropes bingo card with conspiracy tropes, table mid-flip. Mood: Triumphant revelation.

verdict: Fourteen expansion sets, one perfectly constructed rabbit hole — the Worlds Fair Conspiracy TVTropes Kompendium is the most architecturally ambitious deck in the corpus. Named strengths: THE SCISSORS (physically cut the cards to play = destroy the evidence), THE ARCHIVIST (keep artifacts, burn blueprints), KAYFABINGO CARD (flip the table to win). Named weakness: the Beaux-Arts and Fort Geometry sets drop into mechanic-description mode, losing the investigative voice. The font artifact problem (Courier Prime rendering as visible text on ~24 cards) is the only real technical wound. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: A 60-card TVTropes investigation into the 1893 World's Fair mystery — ghost workforces, convenient fires, suppressed patents, and orphan trains organized across 14 named expansion sets. For conspiracy thinkers, history buffs, and anyone who's asked where 75,000 workers went.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: WORLD'S FAIR CONSPIRACY – The TVTropes Investigation Into Where the Workers Went (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

An entire city of white marble rose out of a Chicago swamp in nineteen months, dazzled twenty seven million visitors, and then almost all of it conveniently burned to the ground.

The textbook calls it the White City and files the rest under progress: temporary plaster, cleared on schedule, nothing left to count. Then you ask the small questions the caption skips. Where did the seventy five thousand laborers go when the lights came down. Why did the fireproof palace of the future catch so easily. Who signed the demolition order before anyone could photograph the foundations. The opponent in this deck is not one hidden fact in a vault. It is the tidy caption under the postcard, the one trained to make the question itself feel like bad manners.

World's Fair Conspiracy is Social Story Wrestling aimed at the architecture of the official past. You hold a card, you make the buried case out loud with a straight face, and the table rules whether the caption survives or the foundations start to show. A TVTropes investigation you run with your hands instead of a comment thread.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The World's Fair Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring THE ARCHIVIST, who keeps the receipts the bonfire was meant to erase, THE SCISSORS, the meta-card that turns cutting your own deck into the act of destroying the evidence, and the KAYFABINGO CARD that flips the whole inquiry into a party game when the room gets too solemn to enjoy.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no clearance level, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one law that every card can claim anything until the table calls the bluff.
- The 15-Set Dig: one thread walked from the 1893 White City through the Crystal Palace of 1851, the convenient fires, the orphan trains, the Tesla and Edison current war, and the Paris connection of 1889, fifteen named expansion sets that line up the pieces the official record kept on separate shelves.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
By grabbing this deck you aren't just buying a static PDF. You are entering the Dark Journalism pipeline. Every future thematic expansion and topic-specific deck in this cycle lands in your hands as a free update.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
